task: Linear regression on NYC yellow taxi fare (Q2 2024) using time (hour, day_of_week), trip (trip_distance, passenger_count) and pickup/dropoff borough dummies; outlier filter 0<trip_distance<100, 0<fare_amount<500; test_size=0.2, random_state=42; report RMSE and R2 -> output.json

missing_and_resolved.pyarrow: NOT preinstalled -> installed offline-cached wheel into ./_libs (pyarrow 26.0.1). Downstream MUST do sys.path.insert(0,'./_libs') before importing pyarrow/pandas-parquet.
missing_and_resolved.pyshp / geopandas / fiona / shapely: not preinstalled (shapely 2.2.0 also placed in ./_libs); not required because the shapefile has no .dbf attributes (see taxi_zones section)

data_files.format: parquet (written by parquet-cpp-arrow 14.0.2), all columns ZSTD compressed, no embedded pandas metadata, NO per-column statistics (min/max/null_count absent -> exact null counts require a scan)

columns.name: tpep_dropoff_datetime
columns.role: not used as feature (would leak/undefined); duration optional

columns.name: PULocationID
columns.role: key -> borough_pu_* via taxi zone lookup

columns.name: DOLocationID
columns.role: key -> borough_do_* via taxi zone lookup

columns.name: extra/mta_tax/tip_amount/tolls_amount/improvement_surcharge/total_amount/congestion_surcharge/Airport_fee
columns.role: must NOT be used as features (fare components / leakage)

samples.method: first pyarrow batch (50,000 rows) per file + first row group (1,048,576 rows) for filter/fraction estimates; no full-file dump performed

data_quality.negatives_and_zeros: fare_amount <= 0 in ~1.2-1.6% of rows (min about -393), trip_distance == 0 in ~1.3-1.5% of rows (min 0). The mandated filter 0<fare<500 & 0<dist<100 removes almost all of these.
data_quality.filter_survival_estimate: ~97.26% - 97.46% of rows survive per file (measured on first row group, 1,048,576 rows each). Expected modelling row count approx 10.46M - 10.48M.
data_quality.rare_extremes: trip_distance up to 577 miles and fare up to 850 exist; ~1e-5 fraction is >=100mi or >=500$, so the strict range filter is the main trimming mechanism, not a mass deletion.
data_quality.timestamps_out_of_range: 24 rows total across the 3 files have pickup datetime outside 2024-04-01..2024-07-01 (min 2002-12-31, max 2026-06-26). Negligible (<1e-6) but hour/day_of_week for them is degenerate; safe to keep or drop, document whichever is chosen.
data_quality.nulls: No nulls observed in any column of the sampled row groups (all 19 columns). Note the source schema allows nulls for passenger_count/RatecodeID/others, and parquet has no statistics, so exact null counts were not verified by full scan.
data_quality.passenger_count: ranges 0..8 in samples, ~1.4% zeros; treat as numeric, no clipping required by the spec.
data_quality.location_ids: PULocationID/DOLocationID span 1..265. IDs 264 ('Unknown') and 265 ('Outside of NYC') appear (~0.2-0.5% of dropoffs, ~0.2% of pickups) and have NO borough -> all-zero borough dummies after mapping.
data_quality.duplicate_risk: parquet rows are not deduplicated; duplicates were not quantified (full scan out of scope for inspect node).

taxi_zones.crs: projected, not lon/lat (bbox 913175.11, 120121.88, 1067382.51, 272844.29 - NY State Plane / US-feet style coordinates)
taxi_zones.attribute_table: MISSING - taxi_zones.shp was provided WITHOUT taxi_zones.dbf/.shx, so the .shp carries geometry only (no LocationID/Borough/Zone/service_zone fields). pyshp reports records but there are no attributes to read.
taxi_zones.record_order_verified: record numbers are contiguous 1..263, and geometry positions match the official zone ids: record 1 bbox = far-west small polygon (EWR/Newark Airport, min-x of whole file), record 132 bbox = south-east Queens (JFK Airport), record 138 bbox = north Queens (LaGuardia). Therefore shapefile record i corresponds to LocationID = i.
taxi_zones.borough_mapping_source: taxi_zones/taxi_zone_lookup.csv (ADDED by this node; downloaded from the official TLC source https://d37ci6vzurychx.cloudfront.net/misc/taxi_zone_lookup.csv, 12,331 bytes). Simply read this CSV mapping LocationID -> Borough; a full point-in-polygon spatial join is NOT needed (and would be unreliable without the .dbf/CRS definition).
taxi_zones.locationid_coverage: lookup covers LocationID 1..265 with no duplicates and no gaps in 1..263; ID 264 -> Borough 'Unknown', ID 265 -> Borough NaN (Zone 'Outside of NYC').
taxi_zones.recommended_dummy_note: The 6 boroughs above map onto LocationIDs 1..263 (the polygons that exist in the shapefile). Recommended columns: borough_pu_<Borough> and borough_do_<Borough> (12 features). Unmapped ids (264/265/NaN) become all-zero rows; either keep them as the implicit baseline or dropna on the join. Avoid creating a dummy for 'Unknown'/NaN.

feature_engineering_guidance.day_of_week: tpep_pickup_datetime.dt.dayofweek (pandas: Monday=0..Sunday=6). Data supports 7 distinct values; no weekend-specific handling required.
feature_engineering_guidance.borough_features: 12 dummies (6 boroughs x pickup/dropoff), see taxi_zones.recommended_dummy_note
feature_engineering_guidance.leakage_watch: Do not include total_amount, tip_amount, tolls_amount, extra, mta_tax, congestion_surcharge, Airport_fee, improvement_surcharge, payment_type, RatecodeID or trip duration; the task's feature list excludes them.
feature_engineering_guidance.deterministic_pipeline: pd.concat 3 files -> filter (trip_distance>0)&(trip_distance<100)&(fare_amount>0)&(fare_amount<500) -> build features -> train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42) -> sklearn LinearRegression -> RMSE=sqrt(mse), R2 on the test split.

expected_model_behaviour.note: Not computed here (modeling belongs to a downstream node). Given distance is available, a plain OLS on these 16 features typically reaches R2 around 0.75-0.85 and RMSE of roughly 7-10 USD on Q2 Manhattan-dominated yellow-taxi data; treat as a sanity band, not a result.
caveats: fare_amount includes surcharges/tolls noise that these features cannot explain
borough dummies are coarse (5-6 levels) so intra-borough variation is absorbed by distance/hour
regression on 10.4M rows x 16 columns needs a memory-aware loader: read only the 6 needed columns per file and downcast to float32 if RAM is tight
